# Step 01 — Step-by-Step Instructions

**Generated reference — do not edit this file.**

## Orientation

- Origin: front-left corner of the finished board top.
- +X: right. +Y: rear/toward the arm. +Z: up.
- Confirm FRONT and +Y/rear before placing a part, device, template, or tag.

The image explains order and orientation. Verify all schematic dimensions and hardware against the measured controls below.

## Numbered actions

1. Inspect the blank for damage. Measure and record the front and rear widths, left and right depths, board thickness near every named locator, both corner-to-corner diagonals, local flatness, and overall bow before layout. Accept only 610.0 +/- 0.5 mm width, 457.0 +/- 0.5 mm depth, and 17.50-18.50 mm thickness. Front/rear widths and left/right depths may differ by no more than 0.50 mm. Compute the expected diagonal from the mean measured width and depth; each diagonal must be within 1.00 mm of that value and the two diagonals must be within 1.00 mm of each other. Reject or obtain a controlled engineering disposition before layout if any limit fails.
2. If the board is unsealed, seal both faces and all edges equally and allow the finish to cure fully before taping paper or drilling. If it arrived sealed, verify equal coverage and full cure; do not apply an unnecessary second finish coat.
3. Retrieve the exact Step-00 accepted friendly guide and confirm its recorded path and SHA-256. Do not substitute the overview page, schedule page, assembly-map page, legacy alias, or pages from the other guide after acceptance. If a replacement is printed, repeat Step 00 acceptance and record the new exact file hash before use.
4. For the Letter guide, use pages 4-12 only as the 1:1 drilling field. On a flat surface, arrange the pages in the printed 3 x 3 map, overlap adjacent sheets by exactly the printed 12 mm zones, and align every duplicated registration mark and ID before taping the seams. Never butt sheet edges or unprinted printer margins; that creates a 12 mm error at one seam and a 24 mm cumulative error across two seams. Pages 1-3 are reference pages and must never be punched or drilled from. Skip this tiled-assembly action when using the accepted one-page 24 x 36 inch guide.
5. Before the guide touches the board, remeasure the independent X and Y 100 mm controls on every physical drilling sheet with a steel rule. Both directions on every sheet must be 100.0 +/- 0.2 mm. Reject any page with the wrong scale, missing marks, wrinkling, moisture distortion, stretched tape, or mismatched registration IDs. Scale controls prove print scale only; they are not a released final hole-position tolerance.
6. Place the finished guide on the cured board top. Register the board outline, FRONT, +X/right, and +Y/rear without stretching the paper. Confirm the guide's front-left origin sits at the board's front-left corner and that the opposite board edges, orientation arrow, clamp no-drill area, and tag-only symbols agree before taping the guide to the board.
7. Using drawings/board_hole_coordinates.csv, independently verify all thirteen feature IDs and centers from two directions: X from the left and right-edge remainder, and Y from the front and rear-edge remainder. Do not average conflicting marks. Stop and correct the guide registration if the paper mark and edge measurements disagree. Pay particular attention to PT-HOLD-R1 and PT-HOLD-R2, whose centers are only 21.2 mm from the right board edge; the selected anchor bore, flange, and installation tool still require physical edge-clearance proof.
8. Transfer exactly four blue round locator centers and nine orange square M4 anchor centers with a sharp awl or transfer punch. Do not transfer station outlines, dimensions, registration marks, clamp no-drill shading, or any TAG ONLY / NO DRILL symbol. Photograph the registered guide and all thirteen transferred centers before removing the paper.
9. Remove every paper fragment before drilling, then re-audit all thirteen center punches against drawings/board_hole_coordinates.csv. A printed M4 station/CAD passage reference is not a universal final board bore; the nine orange targets authorize center-punching only until FASTENER_MAP.csv is complete for the actual qualified anchor.
10. Pilot the four locator centers square using the hand-drill guide and a positive depth stop. At each named locator, record local thickness and set the final 6 mm brad-point operation to 15.00 +/- 0.20 mm while also preserving at least 2.00 mm of local board floor. If both conditions cannot be met, stop instead of accepting a thinner floor or underside breakout.
11. Drill the four locator bores only, deburr without enlarging them, measure every actual blind depth, and inspect the underside for breakout before any anchor bore is drilled.
12. Complete FASTENER_MAP.csv for all nine M4 interfaces using the actual anchor maker/part, qualified scrap-board result, selected screw length, bore mode, final board bore, bore depth or through condition, install face, pilot diameter, and qualification reference required by the controlled map. Do not leave a required selection blank and do not infer a bit size from the guide artwork.
13. Only after the complete fastener map is qualified, drill each of the nine final anchor bores square with the recorded pilot/final bits and depth/through control. Protect the two right-edge phone-rail locations from breakout, veneer splitting, and inadequate flange or tool clearance.
14. Install temporary anchors and pins; dry-fit all three stations, all nine retainers, the seam, and the rail-sharing stacks.
15. Only after the complete dry fit passes, epoxy the four locator pins, set and record each named exposed projection at 5.00 +/- 0.15 mm, allow full cure, and repeat the fit checks.
16. Run `(Get-FileHash FASTENER_MAP.csv -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()` from the project root and record the result as board_fabrication_pass.selected_fastener_map_sha256; any later map change reopens this step.
17. Mark FRONT and the revision on the underside; install feet clear of all anchors and reinforcement hardware.

## STOP

> Stop before center transfer or drilling if the board misses any released cut-size, thickness, opposite-edge, diagonal, flatness, or bow limit; any X/Y scale control is wrong; a Letter tile is butted instead of overlapped by 12 mm; registration or edge checks disagree; a station first article is unaccepted; a locator cannot meet both 15.00 +/- 0.20 mm depth and 2.00 mm minimum floor; or any anchor lacks a completed qualified FASTENER_MAP row and scrap-board proof.
